questions.q: What does this lesson say a Technical Architect must decide before designing a single custom object?
options: Which Salesforce edition LTV Global should purchase
Which system is the system of record for each category of data
How many sandboxes the development team will need
Which programming language the integration layer will use
questions.explain: Data architecture starts with deliberately assigning a system of record for each data category, before any object design happens — getting ownership wrong is a classic, expensive enterprise mistake.

questions.q: According to LTV Global's system-of-record map, which system owns general ledger, AP, and AR data?
options: Salesforce
Meridian ERP
LedgerPoint
Snowflake
questions.explain: LedgerPoint remains the system of record for financial transactions, since LTV Global has no appetite to replace its core financial infrastructure as part of this project.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about Salesforce's role as a system of record in this design?
options: Salesforce is deliberately the system of record for everything, including inventory and financial transactions
Salesforce is deliberately NOT the system of record for product/inventory or financial transactions — it owns the customer relationship instead
Salesforce has no system-of-record role at all in this design
Salesforce only stores data that Snowflake has already processed
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly rejects the instinct to make Salesforce the system of record for everything; Meridian keeps owning product/inventory and LedgerPoint keeps owning financial transactions, while Salesforce owns the customer relationship.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe LedgerPoint data that appears in Salesforce, such as 'this account has an overdue invoice'?
options: Full general-ledger line detail, fully replicated into Salesforce
A summarized view — enough for a service rep to act on, without storing full ledger detail in Salesforce
Data that never appears in Salesforce under any circumstances
Raw mainframe batch files stored unprocessed in Salesforce
questions.explain: AR and invoice status are summarized into Salesforce — enough for practical use by reps — without replicating full general-ledger line detail, which stays owned by LedgerPoint alone.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say this data-ownership map is useful during the Chapter 6 Architecture Review Board defense?
options: Because it lets the architect avoid answering any questions about data at all
Because it gives the architect a clean, principled answer (rather than an improvised one) if a board member asks why Salesforce doesn't just store the full ledger
Because ARBs never ask about data ownership
Because the data-ownership map is identical to the risk register
questions.explain: The lesson calls this ownership map one of the most defensible fact patterns in the capstone specifically because it gives a principled, pre-thought-out answer to a predictable ARB question about why Salesforce doesn't replicate the full ledger.
